channel.title: Economic Daily · kaixinguor
channel.description: An economy daily: central banks, growth and the companies that book the profit.

item.title: Economic Daily · November 28, 2026
item.description: This issue starts with two hours on the afternoon of November 27. A State Council readout published before the lunch break promised more market-stabilisation tools and a bigger role for Central Huijin; A-shares opened the afternoon with a vertical rally, ChiNext closed up 11.61% and turnover reached Rmb2.02tn, 52.17% more than the previous day. On the same day, industrial profits for January-October rose 16.0%, with electronics contributing 9.7 percentage points and autos falling 26.0% — prices and profits moved in opposite directions. Elsewhere, local governments issued Rmb4.58tn of new bonds and paid Rmb1.33tn of interest in the first ten months; the PBOC paired “relatively loose” financing conditions with a warning against “blow-ups”. In Europe, French inflation fell to 2.9% while Spain stayed at 4.1%, and the ECB still looks set to hike on December 17; OPEC+ is set to keep Q1 2027 targets, Brent closed at $95.44, and China Shenhua raised HK$6.73bn in a placement to repay debt. Prices move first, profits arrive later, and the debt is paid last. Beijing deploys the “national team” to put a floor under A-shares; ChiNext jumps 11.61% on Rmb2.02tn turnover

item.title: Economic Daily · November 27, 2026
item.description: This issue starts with two balance sheets. The Bank of England cut bank capital requirements by another 30 basis points on November 26, taking system-wide Tier 1 requirements to 12.8% from 13.1% and saying the package could free about £100bn of lending capacity. Its Financial Stability Report also warned that AI-related financing has become complex, circular and opaque, with hyperscaler bond issuance set to exceed $305bn in 2026, or 8% of global investment-grade supply. Across the Atlantic, the US proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies on November 25, with a stacked 20% on China that could rise to 40% and an earliest effective date of January 2027. At home, two price lines moved: fuel prices fell Rmb440 and Rmb425 a tonne from midnight, the seventh cut this year, and the new services-trade plan split producer and consumer services into two tracks, with 25 tasks. In industry, an attack on Saudi Arabia's Jizan refinery lifted Brent by 2.07% to $96.57; Kelai Mechatronics got an exchange letter after five limit-ups; and China Merchants Shekou moved Rmb19bn of its own cash into Nanyou.Capital rules, tariffs and oil: three balance sheets repriced on the same day. Bank of England cuts bank capital requirements by 30bp and says it can free about £100bn for lending

item.title: Economic Daily · November 26, 2026
item.description: This issue is about duration. US core PCE inflation rose to 3.3% in October, the highest since November 2023, with headline at 3.8%; the same morning BEA revised third-quarter GDP growth up to a 4.3% annual rate, and markets now treat a 25bp hike on December 8-9 as settled — with a pause off the table, every long-duration asset has to be repriced. The same day, the European Parliament passed the last annual budget of the EU's 2021-2027 framework: €199.7bn in commitments against €211.5bn in payments, the €11.8bn gap being earlier promises coming due. In corporate finance, the five biggest US cloud providers spent $556.9bn on capex in nine months, more than their $542.9bn of operating cash flow, and funded the difference with debt; S&P put Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch Negative while five-year protection on CoreWeave debt briefly cost 15.34 percentage points a year; and the spot price of compute is falling — SpaceX cut Blackwell cluster rents by 20% to 35%, and the 50,000 H200s Anthropic declined to renew are being marketed about 23% below market. In China, listed public REITs reached 100 with Rmb264.27bn raised as the first private-developer retail REIT listed; Poly Developments took up to Rmb20bn of 10-year unsecured bonds to its board, first use repaying interest-bearing debt; and five ministries wired aid-fund performance grades into next year's allocation formula.The interest rate is the denominator: whoever lengthens duration pays interest on every year that follows. US core PCE rises to 3.3% in October, a near three-year high, as markets price a December hike

item.title: Economic Daily · November 25, 2026
item.description: This issue is about the price of money and where it goes. November 25 is a reserve-requirement settlement day, the week's peak for net government-bond payments, and the day Rmb1tn of MLF and Rmb80bn of treasury cash deposits mature. The central bank meets the short end with Rmb500bn of seven-day reverse repos and the long end with Rmb800bn of MLF against that Rmb1tn — a net Rmb200bn drain of one-year money. Quantity at seven days, shrinkage at one year: one operation re-pairs the maturity of the banking system's funding. On policy, Brussels will impose provisional safeguard measures on imported hybrid cars from December 1, having opened the case on October 30, and MOFCOM reserves the right to WTO dispute settlement and trade compensation; the National Data Administration writes 12.5% of GDP for core digital industries by 2030 into a five-year plan; MIIT hands a 6G pilot to eight provinces and municipalities. In industry, China Mobile tenders 20,480 AI accelerator cards and one integrator takes 2,048 of them at a Rmb11.666bn bid, while Wall Street reprices AI hardware with a 7.88% one-day fall in the Philadelphia semiconductor index.A reverse repo is a liability, a safeguard is a gate, a tender share is an order: none of the three touches this quarter's income statement, and all three set next year's cash flow. PBOC to inject Rmb500bn of seven-day repos and Rmb800bn of MLF on November 25, draining Rmb200bn of long-term liquidity

item.title: Economic Daily · November 24, 2026
item.description: This issue is about whose balance sheet ends up holding the assets. Insurers finished the third quarter with Rmb41.63tn of investable assets, of which Rmb20.73tn — 51.5% of invested assets — sat in bonds, more than Rmb800bn added in the quarter alone, alongside Rmb146.5bn of net equity buying. The marginal buyer of ultra-long paper is an insurance liability, not a trading desk. On the fiscal side Rmb4.13tn of this year's special-purpose bonds are already away, 93% of the quota, and the 2027 limit may be pre-allocated at the full 60% ceiling: next year's money sold in this year's fourth quarter. Offshore, the PBOC sold Rmb50bn of bills in Hong Kong at 1.32% for three months and 1.41% for a year, putting a price floor under offshore renminbi. The two ends of the price spectrum then did the same thing by different means: supply was rationed by decree — Congo (DRC) suspends all cobalt exports from November 30 and Chinese electronic cobalt jumped 11.95% — while a balance sheet absorbed the shock, with Nvidia adding $952bn of market value in a day, a record.Market value is not money and a quota is not output: keep the two apart and you can see who actually paid. Insurers' investable assets reach Rmb41.63tn, with bonds at 51.5% and a Rmb800bn quarterly build

item.title: Economic Daily · November 23, 2026
item.description: This issue is about who sets the price of liquidity. On Sunday evening the exchanges cut the minimum margin ratio back to 80% from 100%, so the same collateral now carries 25% more position, and paired that with ChiNext market-maker rules and Rmb2.758bn of fee reductions. None of it prints money; all of it lowers the price of trading and leverage. Seoul wrote the same story in a harder key: after KOSPI fell more than 5% in a session, the government put its KRW515bn stabilisation fund on deployment standby, eased buyback filing limits and tightened short-selling surveillance — administrative buyers standing in for private ones who are leaving. The bank data show the bill: a 1.41% net interest margin held up by deposit repricing, and an NPL ratio that rose 2bp. Copper turns tariff expectations into a map of inventories, with 94% of exchange stocks sitting in the US and the Yangshan premium at a record $500 a tonne.Liquidity is never free: it is paid for either by a price or by somebody's balance sheet. Margin ratio cut back to 80% from November 30, with ChiNext market makers floated and Rmb2.758bn of new fee cuts

item.title: Economic Daily · November 22, 2026
item.description: This issue is about the gap between a quoted price and a traded one. Spot gold fell to about $3,500 an ounce on November 21, a 14-month low, down nearly 9% on the week and roughly 36% from its January peak — yet Chinese jewellery brands have cut their per-gram tags by only a little over Rmb600 from the year's high. Cement makers sent out price-increase letters of Rmb20 to Rmb80 a tonne this month while the national average was still falling week on week. The SCFI slipped just 1.9%, but the US west coast fell 5.6% and South America 20-foot boxes 15.2%; the route-by-route split says the front-loading is over more clearly than the composite does. On the policy side, the PBOC will auction Rmb50bn of bills in Hong Kong to add points to the offshore renminbi curve, the NDRC is chasing both fund payments and physical work volume, and the battery consumption tax has put a 2%-to-4% timetable between cell makers and carmakers.A price is not a number printed on a quote sheet; it is the outcome of a negotiation, and whoever holds the leverage pushes the tax, the freight and the cost onto somebody else. Spot gold slides to about $3,500, a 14-month low, as Chinese jewellery tags fall just over Rmb600 a gram from the peak

item.title: Economic Daily · November 21, 2026
item.description: Two price chains repriced at once. In the United States, the Nasdaq fell 5.28% and Nvidia about 14% on November 20, leaving the Dow and the S&P 500 more than 10% below their recent highs — even as the 10-year Treasury yield dropped 12 basis points to 4.92% and the odds of a December hike slipped from 100% to 91.4%. The discount rate eased; the cash flows did not. In China, budget revenue for January–October rose 4.9% to Rmb19.57tn while spending rose just 1% and land-sale revenue fell 25.8%; the same day the Shanghai Composite lost 1.23%, the SSE 50 gained 0.45% and the four big state banks closed at year highs. In industry, NetEase's games revenue fell 1.7% and its Hong Kong shares dropped as much as 19%, while the Global Electronics Association warned that PCB orders rose 56.1% against 13.3% shipment growth, with shortages running at least into the first half of 2027.Risk premia, not policy rates, did the repricing: one pool of money, four prices — for equity, government debt, land and factory capacity. Nasdaq falls 5.28% and Nvidia about 14%, leaving the Dow and S&P 500 more than 10% below their recent highs

item.title: Economic Daily · November 20, 2026
item.description: Three prices for money, on one day. China left the loan prime rate unchanged for an 18th month — 3.0% at one year and 3.5% at five and above — while the central bank supplied Rmb379.5bn of overnight reverse repos at 1.25%. The finance ministry sold $2bn of three-year dollar bonds in Hong Kong at 4.821%, covered 36 times. Japan's October core inflation ran at 2.2% and swaps put an 86% chance on a December hike. In the United States, jobless claims came in at 203,000 and the Philadelphia Fed index dropped from 20.9 to 6.3. On the corporate side, Anthropic ended its first session up 17.07% after an $81.3bn IPO, Pinduoduo reported flat revenue of Rmb108.3bn with Rmb29.5bn of profit, and Alibaba grew revenue 10% with adjusted EBITA up 260%.The policy rate is frozen, the cross-currency spread is widening and equity risk is being repriced — the same money, quoted differently by duration, and the longest balance sheets feel it first. China leaves the LPR unchanged for an 18th month at 3.0% and 3.5%, with overnight repo still at 1.25%

item.title: Economic Daily · November 19, 2026
item.description: Two prices for money, on the same day. The October FOMC minutes show almost every official thought further increases would be needed; two raised the possibility of more than 25 basis points in December, and futures now fully price 25 in December and another 25 in January. The euro area's October inflation was confirmed at 4.0%, with energy running at 21.0%. China priced the other end of the curve: Rmb150bn of seven-year recapitalisation bonds cleared at 1.40%, only 15 basis points over three-year paper, while Shanghai and Shenzhen turnover shrank to Rmb1.37trn, a 16-month low. In industry, Tencent spent Rmb81.4bn of capex against Rmb63.6bn of net profit and saw gross margin slip to 56%; WTI settled at $83.26, down 3.2%, and LME copper fell 3.91%.One market is pricing risk with higher rates; the other is pricing seven-year money at 1.40%. Both are asking whose balance sheet lasts longer. Fed minutes: almost every official saw further hikes ahead, and two floated more than 25 basis points in December

item.title: Economic Daily · November 18, 2026
item.description: One price governs the short end. The PBOC lent Rmb700.2bn overnight at 1.25% on November 18 and drained a net Rmb13.8bn against maturities; the finance ministry's Rmb650m market-making sale cleared two- and three-year paper at the same 1.25% — overnight, two years and three years pinned to a single level. Pricing shifted elsewhere too. US retail sales rose just 0.2% in October against 0.8% in September, and the three main indexes fell more than 1%, the Dow down 848.75 points with financials and utilities leading. In industry, Nvidia reported $115.8bn of quarterly revenue, up 103%, guided to $130bn and cut its gross-margin outlook to 71-72%; JD.com grew revenue 3.5% to Rmb309.6bn and swung to a Rmb5.2bn operating profit. When the front end is pinned, the long end has to be priced on something else. PBOC injects Rmb700.2bn of overnight cash at 1.25% and drains Rmb13.8bn net against Rmb714bn of maturities

item.title: Economic Daily · November 17, 2026
item.description: Three numbers landed badly this week, each for a different reason. October industrial output still grew 4.8% from a year earlier, yet fixed-asset investment fell 8.1%, with real estate development down 21.6%. Producer prices rose 5.7% while consumer prices rose 0.7% — costs are climbing, selling prices are not, and the five-point gap is being carried by companies in the middle of the chain. In the same window the finance ministry put Rmb650m of market-making support behind two- and three-year government bonds to repair quote continuity, the car association turned a 60-day payment pledge from 17 automakers into an annual audit that samples at least 15 suppliers apiece, and Victory Giant laid Rmb70.7bn of bank credit lines on the table to pre-fund capacity in Malaysia. Supply, prices and payment terms all end up on the same cash-flow statement. October industrial output grows 4.8% while fixed investment falls 8.1%, and producer prices outrun consumer prices by five points

item.title: Economic Daily · November 16, 2026
item.description: Three ledgers closed over one weekend: a strait, an exchange, a courtroom. The Strait of Hormuz is still shut — two tankers struck mines on November 15, and the UN puts fertiliser prices about 30% above pre-war levels, with 45 million people at risk of acute food insecurity if another planting season is lost. In the same week the Beijing Stock Exchange turned five with 355 listed companies, roughly Rmb800bn of market value and daily turnover that has climbed from under Rmb1bn to almost Rmb20bn, while the securities regulator put market-stability mechanics, quant trading and share sales on its research list. And a Dutch court handed Wingtech a penalty ceiling of EUR300m, moving the fate of Nexperia from negotiation to litigation. Price, liquidity and control, each priced on its own terms. Hormuz stays shut: two tankers hit mines, and fertiliser prices are already about 30% above pre-war levels

item.title: Economic Daily · November 15, 2026
item.description: This issue asks who is still borrowing. The central bank's October credit report opens the ledger: social financing rose Rmb28.61trn in ten months, Rmb2.29trn less than a year earlier, held up by Rmb11.49trn of net government bond issuance, while household loans fell Rmb1.46trn and household deposits rose Rmb8.47trn. The same day the PBoC trimmed its six-month outright reverse repo to Rmb200bn, draining a net Rmb300bn across both tenors in November, and US October PPI inflation of 6.5%, the highest since November 2022, made a December hike the consensus. Money is shrinking in quantity; its price is being re-marked in two directions at once. Social financing stock grows 7.2% and M2 7.1%, but ten-month issuance is Rmb2.29trn below last year

item.title: Economic Daily · November 13, 2026
item.description: Two hands reached in opposite directions today. At the Shanghai Stock Exchange's international investors conference the CSRC put three auditable numbers on the table: Rmb100bn of the third swap-facility tranche already deployed, more than Rmb600bn of A-shares bought by long-term money this year, and dividends plus buybacks now larger than IPO and refinancing proceeds. Hours later the NDRC cut petrol and diesel by Rmb645 and Rmb625 a tonne, while Brent rose 3.3% to US$95.82. One hand holds up the price of assets with rules; the other presses down the cost of energy. Both bills land on household balance sheets. CSRC: Rmb100bn of the third swap facility is deployed as long-term money buys over Rmb600bn of A-shares

item.title: Economic Daily · November 12, 2026
item.description: Today the price of money is being re-anchored. The PBOC's quarterly report wants loan pricing to move past a single LPR reference, with DR001 averaging 1.34% in the first nine months and new corporate loans just under 3.0%; the same session, a 63-day T-bill cleared at 1.05%, 20bp under the 1.25% overnight repo rate. Assets split behind it: ChiNext added 3.11%, the Hang Seng lost 0.98%. When the front end is pinned, whoever holds the duration pays for the price. PBOC Q3 report: loan pricing to move beyond a single LPR reference as DR001 averages 1.34%

item.title: Economic Daily · November 11, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is that the price of money moved first and assets re-sorted behind it. US October CPI came in above forecasts, markets priced a December hike at 100%, and the dollar and short-dated Treasuries rose together. The same evening, Alibaba put T-Head on a path to a Hong Kong listing, TSMC approved a $40.9bn capital budget, and the CIIE closed with $85.45bn of intended deals. The funding window is narrowing; only assets that can fund themselves get to negotiate. US October CPI rises 0.4% m/m, above forecasts: markets price a December hike at 100%

item.title: Economic Daily · November 10, 2026
item.description: Short money is being drained while long money comes due. The People's Bank of China lent only RMB 190bn overnight on November 10, after a RMB 44bn net drain the previous day, and November brings RMB 1.8tn of maturing MLF and outright reverse repos plus more than RMB 1.5tn of net government bond financing. On the same day, savings bonds opened at 1.63% and 1.7%, oil fell as much as 5.6%, October passenger car retail was down 27.1%, and one Nasdaq-100 ETF traded 21% above its net asset value. The price of money has not moved; the tenor at which you can get it has. Overnight reverse repos keep draining: RMB 190bn lent on November 10, with RMB 1.8tn of MLF and outright repos maturing in November

item.title: Economic Daily · November 9, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is upstream heat, downstream cold, and money looking for an exit in between. October CPI rose 0.7% year on year and PPI 5.7%, a five-point scissors gap: fresh vegetables at -16.9% and pork at -8.6% held consumer prices down, while coal at +36.6% and oil and gas at +35.0% pushed producer prices up. The same day, central SOEs signed more than $100bn at the import expo, and Japan's finance ministry disclosed ¥15.4tn of intervention in three days. The price split will end up as a redistribution on income statements. China's October CPI rises 0.7% y/y and PPI 5.7%, a five-point scissors gap

item.title: Economy Daily · November 8, 2026
item.description: Today's thread is that the story is running ahead of the ledger. Economic Daily took aim at solid-state battery marketing: Ouyang Minggao says everything claimed as industrialised is still a hybrid, the fastest sulphide route sits at TRL5, and the target for all-solid-state scale is 2030. Meanwhile Berkshire piled cash up to $377.4bn and bought back $9.6bn of stock, the Africa-China trade forum signed RMB 40.96bn of projects, and Shanghai's state-owned buyers placed $2.862bn of import-expo orders. Technology runs on TRL time; capital runs on quarterly time. Two regulators target online financial black markets, naming debt-avoidance, insurance-refund and credit-repair accounts
